extends: the v1 research files, which are not modified
grade_policy: No feeding grade is assigned in the research layer. A record here is not a statement that the plant is safe to feed.

sources.citation: Lagarde, F., Bonnet, X., Corbin, J., Henen, B., Nagy, K., Mardonov, B., Naulleau, G. 2003. Foraging behaviour and diet of an ectothermic herbivore: Testudo horsfieldi. Ecography 26:236-242.
sources.method: continuous focal observation of 7 wild tortoises per period; plant availability from 17 (mating period) and 10 (post-mating period) quadrats
sources.what_was_read: whole article from the authors' institute copy; Tables 1-2 on p. 240. The text layer prints table columns out of order, so a percentage is transcribed only where Hunter's index (diet share / availability) fixes which number is which

sources.citation: Moll, D., Klemens, M.W. 1996. Ecological Characteristics of the Pancake Tortoise, Malacochersus tornieri, in Tanzania. Chelonian Conservation and Biology 2(1):26-35.
sources.method: analysis of fecal material from occupied crevices and newly caught tortoises, and direct observation of foraging animals
sources.what_was_read: abstract, methods and the 'Diet and Access to Water' section on pp. 31-32, read from the scanned page image

sources.citation: Bayley, J.R., Highfield, A.C. 1996. Observations on Ecological Changes Threatening a Population of Testudo graeca graeca in the Souss Valley, Southern Morocco. Chelonian Conservation and Biology 2(1):36-42.
sources.method: field visits from 1992; Table 1 lists plants seen in the habitat that the authors call known to be palatable, from observation of grazing wild tortoises and of captive tortoises in Morocco; farmers' reports for crops
sources.what_was_read: the 'Dietary Modifications' section and Table 1 on pp. 40-41, read from the scanned page image; the page range is inferred from the printed page numbers of a 7-page PDF

sources.citation: Lambert, M.R.K. 1993. On Growth, Sexual Dimorphism, and the General Ecology of the African Spurred Tortoise, Geochelone sulcata, in Mali. Chelonian Conservation and Biology 1(1):37-46.
sources.method: field visits and measurement of confiscated and village-held tortoises, October-November 1991
sources.what_was_read: habitat and discussion passages on feeding, pp. 41 and 44; the page range is inferred from the printed page numbers of a 10-page PDF

sources.citation: Platt, S.G., Saw Tun Khaing, Win Ko Ko, Kalyar. 2001. A Tortoise Survey of Shwe Settaw Wildlife Sanctuary, Myanmar, with Notes on the Ecology of Geochelone platynota and Indotestudo elongata. Chelonian Conservation and Biology 4(1), Notes and Field Reports.
sources.method: field survey in August 1999 with hunter interviews; two scats examined
sources.what_was_read: the food-habits paragraph on the fourth page of the PDF; the journal page numbers were not confirmed

sources.citation: Oftedal, O.T., Hillard, S., Morafka, D.J. 2002. Selective Spring Foraging by Juvenile Desert Tortoises (Gopherus agassizii) in the Mojave Desert: Evidence of an Adaptive Nutritional Strategy. Chelonian Conservation and Biology 4(2):341-352.
sources.method: bite counts on 15 juvenile tortoises foraging on natural vegetation inside the FISS enclosure, 24 April - 1 May 1998; laboratory analysis of the plant parts eaten
sources.what_was_read: Tables 3, 4 and 6 on pp. 345 and 347, read from the scanned page images; the page range is inferred from the printed page numbers of a 12-page PDF

sources.citation: Pillajo Montesdeoca, P.S. 2020. Descripción inicial de la dieta de la tortuga gigante de la Isla Santiago (Chelonoidis darwini), Galápagos, Ecuador. Disertación de Licenciatura, Pontificia Universidad Católica del Ecuador, Quito.
sources.method: seeds and plant remains separated from 18 feces samples collected in the dry season in the arid and humid zones; plants identified mainly from seeds
sources.what_was_read: abstract, results pp. 15-21 and Anexos 9-10 (pp. 55-59 of the thesis). The annex rows were taken from the PDF text layer by a script and the row counts (75 arid, 34 humid) were checked against the thesis
sources.rows_not_transcribed: 19 morphotype rows without a genus or species name ('Tipo ...')

sources.citation: Moorhouse-Gann, R.J., Vaughan, I.P., Cole, N.C. et al. 2022. Impacts of herbivory by ecological replacements on an island ecosystem. Journal of Applied Ecology 59(9):2245-2261.
sources.method: DNA metabarcoding of 80 dung samples (March-July 2015), morphological examination of 50 dung samples and 212 feeding observations of Aldabra giant tortoises introduced on Round Island
sources.what_was_read: abstract, methods, results and Table 3 (pp. 10-11 of the article). Table 3 was taken from the PDF text layer by a script; each count was assigned to its column by checking count / sample size against the printed frequency. The author list is given as printed on the repository cover page

column_totals_checked.discrepancy_note: The metabarcoding and observation columns match the printed totals. The dung-morphology column gives 23 taxa here against 21 printed; the cause was not found, so the dung-morphology counts are less certain than the others.

sources.citation: Ellis-Soto, D., Blake, S., Soultan, A., Guézou, A., Cabrera, F., Lötters, S. 2017. Plant species dispersed by Galapagos tortoises surf the wave of habitat suitability under anthropogenic climate change. PLoS ONE 12(7):e0181333.
sources.method: seed counts in 222 tortoise dung piles (159 La Reserva, 63 Cerro Fatal) collected 2009-2013 along two elevation gradients
sources.what_was_read: abstract, methods and results of the open-access article

sources.citation: Figueroa, A., Chernyavskiy, P., Greenacre, M., Herrera, A., Cuni, L., Villate, J., Galetti, M., Liu, H., Whitfield, S. 2024. Precipitation Drives Frugivory in a Subtropical Generalist Herbivore, the Gopher Tortoise, and Alters Its Functional Role as a Seed Disperser. Ecology and Evolution 14(11):e70585.
sources.method: intact seeds identified in 207 fecal samples
sources.what_was_read: abstract, methods, Table 2 and discussion of the open-access article. Table 2 was taken from the page text by a script

sources.citation: De la Ossa V., J., Guevara-Riaño, L., Horta-Orozco, L.D., Martínez-Mendoza, D. 2009. Influencia del color en el comportamiento alimentario de Geochelone (Chelonoidis) carbonaria (Spix 1824) en cautiverio. Revista Colombiana de Ciencia Animal 1(2):157-167.
sources.method: 20 captive adults in two enclosures; flowers of ten plants offered fresh to one group and dried to the other at 2% of live weight every three days; time to reach and time to consume recorded

sources.citation: Długosz, J., Rawski, M., Kierończyk, B., Józefiak, D. 2015. Wstępne badanie preferencji żywieniowych żółwi stepowych (Testudo horsfieldii) w warunkach chowu terraryjnego. Nauka Przyroda Technologie 9(4):#60.
sources.method: free-choice feeding of eight adult tortoises in a terrarium for six weeks: six herbs, six fruits and six vegetables, two weeks each; refusals weighed

sources.citation: Sriprateep, K., Aranyavalai, V., Aowphol, A., Thirakhupt, K. 2013. Population Structure and Reproduction of the Elongated Tortoise Indotestudo elongata (Blyth, 1853) at Ban Kok Village, Northeastern Thailand. Tropical Natural History 13(1):21-37.
sources.method: direct observation of free-living tortoises in and around a village, May 2007 - August 2009
